elements.problem: Pulse<50, unable to speak, silent chest (tight and no wheeze), PEFR<33%, drowsy, acute confusion all present as OR inside an AND with wheeze/tight chest, priority Emergency. SNOMED concepts verified to exist.
evidence: Emergency: life-threatening wheeze/tight chest :: (or (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Pulse, function" "observable entity") bpm) 50) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unable to speak" "finding")) (and (clinical_finding Tight chest) (no (clinical_finding Wheezing))) (< (measurement PEFR ratio %) 33) Drowsy Acute confusion)

elements.problem: Life threatening -> Emergency priority; trigger present.
evidence: Emergency: life-threatening wheeze/tight chest :: (or (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Pulse, function" "observable entity") bpm) 50) (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Unable to speak" "finding")) (and (clinical_finding Tight chest) (no (clinical_finding Wheezing))) (< (measurement PEFR ratio %) 33) Drowsy Acute confusion)

elements.problem: All six severe criteria encoded with right thresholds/directions. Minor: SpO2 uses the generic 'Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen' rather than Peripheral oxygen saturation; acceptable.
evidence: Urgent: severe wheeze/tight chest :: (or (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen" "observable entity") %) 90) (> RR bpm 30) (> Pulse bpm 120) Unable to complete a sentence in one breath (< PEFR % 60) Feeling agitated)

Urgent: severe wheeze/tight chest :: (or (< (measurement (snomed_concept "Hemoglobin saturation with oxygen" "observable entity") %) 90) (> RR bpm 30) (> Pulse bpm 120) Unable to complete a sentence in one breath (< PEFR % 60) Feeling agitated)

parts_missing: Heart failure likely: 'patient >= 50 years with first episode of wheeze/tight chest' (second OR branch) is not encoded; no age criterion and no first-episode criterion anywhere in the heart failure rule or check_for
elements.problem: Anaphylaxis bullet fully encoded (sudden wheeze/tight chest AND any of itch/rash, face/tongue swelling, SBP<90, DBP<60, dizziness, collapse, abdominal pain, vomiting, drug/food exposure, insect bite/sting) as a possible diagnosis. Heart failure rule encodes only orthopnea AND leg swelling; the page's 'or' branch (age >= 50 and first episode) is lost.
evidence: Diagnose possible anaphylaxis from sudden wheeze/tight chest :: (and (or sudden Wheezing / sudden Tight chest) (or Generalized pruritus ... Insect sting))
Diagnose probable heart failure from wheeze/tight chest :: (and (or Wheezing Tight chest) (clinical_finding Orthopnea) (clinical_finding Leg swelling symptom))

rule_level_problems.rule: Diagnose probable heart failure from wheeze/tight chest
rule_level_problems.problem: Page says '(orthopnea AND leg swelling) OR (age >= 50 with first episode)'. Rule has only the first branch, so older first-episode patients never get heart failure likely. The first-episode part may be hard to express, but age >= 50 with a first-episode proxy could be a second rule or flagged as not representable.

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for wheeze/tight chest severity and causes (check_for)
rule_level_problems.problem: check_for lacks any age >= 50 / first-episode item needed for heart failure; BP < 90/60, pulse, RR, SpO2 and PEFR are covered only by measurement criteria in rules, not check_for (acceptable).

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: severe wheeze/tight chest vs Urgent: wheeze/tight chest
rule_level_problems.problem: Both are Urgent, so the severe rule is redundant with the catch-all urgent rule; severity distinction (mild/moderate vs severe) is not represented. Page does head the whole box 'give urgent attention', so Urgent for all is defensible.
Silent chest encoded as Tight chest AND NOT Wheezing under an outer wheeze-or-tight-chest requirement: logically correct. No problem found; noted as checked.

summary: The red-box triage logic (Emergency life-threatening criteria and Urgent severe criteria) is encoded correctly with verified SNOMED concepts and right thresholds; the anaphylaxis possible rule is also complete. The most consequential gap is the heart failure probable rule, which omits the page's second branch (age >= 50 with first episode of wheeze/tight chest). Management steps and time-based reassessment branches are out of scope by design.
